page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical Intel Xeon 8369HB cores running at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptography standards like AES. In benchmark evaluations, the processor demonstrates solid mid-range performance, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 8021.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 17307.79. Single-core performance is characterized by a Geekbench single-core score of 1268.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1562.49.

Memory performance is robust for cached operations, reaching a read-only small block bandwidth of 927.07 GB/sec, though uncached large block operations drop to 64.29 GB/sec for reads and 38.96 GB/sec for writes. The instance handles high-throughput workloads efficiently, as evidenced by a static web serving throughput of 12.68 GB/sec and a Redis SET performance of 15.27 million operations per second. For machine learning tasks, the CPU can process small 135M parameter LLM prompts at 962.14 tokens per second, but performance degrades significantly on larger models, with 7B parameter prompt processing dropping to a weak 23.28 tokens per second.

Given its high clock speed and compute-to-memory ratio, the ecs.hfc7.4xlarge is highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for software compilation, web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and database operations.

Built on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor, it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. The instance supports AVX-512 instructions, enabling efficient execution of vector and matrix operations. Benchmark results place its performance in the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8021.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 17307.79. It demonstrates strong capabilities in static web serving at 12.68 GB/sec and Redis operations at 15.27 million operations per second. However, memory-intensive uncached operations and larger LLM inference tasks show performance limitations. This instance is best suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
